skill.author: DammianMiller

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences and TypeScript examples. The only confirmed risk is the checklist guidance to make npm lint and test scripts pass, because project-controlled npm scripts can execute arbitrary commands in untrusted repositories.

remediation.issue: Checklist implies running npm scripts without an explicit trust check.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running `npm run lint` or `npm run test`, especially in untrusted repositories.

content.value_statement: TypeScript and Node.js projects often suffer from weak typing, slow async code, and inconsistent CLI patterns. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward strict, maintainable implementations.
actual_capabilities: Defines strict TypeScript compiler settings for NodeNext projects.
Shows safer alternatives to any using unknown, generics, and type guards.
Recommends async patterns, streaming, and generator-based processing for performance.
Provides CLI structure patterns using Commander.js, typed options, and clear error handling.
Covers Vitest setup, coverage thresholds, mocking, and review checklist items.
limitations: It is a guidance-only skill and does not inspect a repository by itself.
Examples are illustrative and may need adaptation to project frameworks.
It does not replace security review for generated filesystem, database, or network code.
It assumes modern Node.js and strict TypeScript conventions.

use_cases.title: Harden a TypeScript Library
use_cases.description: Package maintainers can align tsconfig, exports, tests, and public types with strict TypeScript expectations.

use_cases.title: Build a Reliable CLI
use_cases.description: CLI developers can structure commands, options, validation, progress, and failure handling for Node.js tools.

use_cases.title: Review Backend Changes
use_cases.description: Engineering reviewers can check async behavior, null safety, tests, and maintainability before merging TypeScript changes.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Strict TypeScript
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Node.js project setup. Recommend strict TypeScript settings, module options, and missing scripts before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Function Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this TypeScript function for explicit return types, null safety, and clear errors. Preserve the current behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Typed CLI
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Commander.js CLI for this workflow. Include command structure, typed options, validation strategy, and test coverage plan.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Performance and Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript Node.js module for async bottlenecks, memory risk, dependency boundaries, and testing gaps. Prioritize concrete fixes.

output_examples.input: A CLI command currently parses options manually and exits on every error.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend Commander.js command definitions, typed option parsing, a reusable error boundary, and tests for validation failures.

output_examples.input: A data import loads a large file before processing records.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest streaming, pipeline-based transforms, bounded concurrency, and tests for malformed input and partial failures.

output_examples.input: A service uses loose types and returns inconsistent errors.
output_examples.output: The skill would propose unknown inputs with type guards, explicit return types, Result objects for expected failures, and custom errors for unexpected failures.

best_practices: Ask for repository-specific constraints, supported Node.js versions, and package module format before applying patterns.
Pair generated code with type checking, linting, and tests from the target project.
Review filesystem, database, and network examples before using them in production code.
anti_patterns: Treating sample snippets as complete production code without validation, authorization, or error handling.
Using the skill to bypass local project style, framework conventions, or maintainer requirements.
Applying strict compiler settings without planning incremental migration for large legacy projects.

faq.question: Does this skill run code?
faq.answer: No. It provides Markdown guidance and TypeScript examples for an AI coding assistant.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it create a full CLI?
faq.answer: It can guide design and implementation, but the assistant still needs project files and requirements.

faq.question: Does it support CommonJS?
faq.answer: The guidance favors modern NodeNext and ESM. CommonJS projects may need adapted settings.

faq.question: Is it safe for production code?
faq.answer: It is useful for production guidance, but generated code still needs review, tests, and security checks.

faq.question: Why were security findings reported?
faq.answer: Static analysis flagged Markdown backticks and illustrative APIs. Manual review found no executable behavior in the skill file.
